name: Fewest jumps
brief:
`nums[i]` is the longest jump you can make from position `i`, and you may jump any shorter distance. Start at position 0. Return the fewest jumps that reach the last position, or -1 if you cannot. A list of one or no entries needs 0 jumps.

Write `min_jumps(nums)`.

Example. For `nums = [1, 1, 1, 1]` each jump moves one place, so reaching position 3 takes 3 jumps.
constraints: $O(n)$ time is the target. Trying every earlier position is too slow.
All tests share a 5-second time limit.
hint: Keep the furthest place reachable so far. When you reach the end of the current jump, you must take another, to that furthest place.

examples.note: Jump from 0 to position 3, which holds a 3, then jump 3 places to the end: 2 jumps.
Each entry is 1, so every jump moves one place and the end needs 3 jumps.

how: Submit runs 11 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: `end` marks the last position the current number of jumps can reach.
`far` marks the furthest position one more jump could reach from anywhere inside that range.
Reaching `end` forces a jump to `far`. If `far` has not moved, the end is out of reach.
